authority: Owner request to populate the existing ORI source collections in Russian and English; later instruction limits concurrent research workers to avoid excessive usage.
scope: The 144 programme-level entries in the thirteen current public research maps: 39 book entries, 66 studies/resources, 39 researchers/teams. Some sources recur across programmes. Earlier review bibliographies remain separate.
method: Inspect the existing maps and preserve entry ordering and programme scope.
Check primary publisher, author, paper, data and institutional sources in bounded batches.
Write paired source analyses distinguishing source claims, ORI interpretation, limits and actual reading depth.
For books, target extended analysis of roughly 20–30 conventional pages only after enough lawful source text is inspected; never count an abstract-based description as full reading.
Record full-text requirements separately from openly available texts that still require close reading.
Verify coverage, bilingual structure, links, reader routes, source attribution and public/private boundaries.
Save provenance and exact release state; never infer successful deployment from a commit alone.
public_boundary: Only already public source maps and public third-party information are used. No unpublished private research methods or original hypotheses are imported.
limitations: Internal AI-assisted editorial checks are not external scientific peer review.
No experiments or numerical results are independently reproduced in initial source analyses.
A reachable source is not necessarily a fully read source.
Source access and factual corrections are recorded per entry; old map dates do not substitute for current verification.
date_basis: UTC; stable task/branch identifiers may contain the originally assigned 2026-10-25 label.
